Home / Start a portal

Start with what is already public.

The canonical instructions live in the Better LGU guide. This page is a short reading copy of those steps, with the source linked rather than rewritten as our own advice.

Six steps from intent to upkeep

  1. Define the portal

    A Better LGU portal is a publicly accessible site that makes local information easy to find. You do not need permission from the LGU to start one.

  2. Register the intent

    Register the planned portal in the community directory with the status recorded upstream as “Planned”, using a public pull request.

  3. Use a community template

    The guide points builders to existing community templates rather than starting from a blank page.

  4. Gather public data

    Collect information that is already public, budgets, projects, directories and other local records, and organise it so residents can find it.

  5. Use the advised address pattern

    The guide recommends the better[lguname].org address pattern for a local portal.

  6. Deploy, then update the status

    Publish the portal, then update its directory entry from planned to active. Keep the information current: the guide asks maintainers to update at least quarterly.

What the register means

Entries in the directory use four statuses: Active, Work in Progress, Unmaintained and Planned. Two secondary tags may also appear: Stale and Open for Adoption.

“Open for Adoption” marks an entry where the community is looking for someone to take over. It is an open call, not a claim that a portal is broken.

Read the full Better LGU guide

Look at what exists

Check the directory first: a portal may already exist for the place you have in mind. If none does, the upstream register accepts new entries through a public contribution.
